chunks: And it was narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A man was found with a woman in a house, and she admitted that she was his wife, and he admitted that he was her husband.”
So he عليه السلام said: “There may be a man whom, if he were brought to me, I would allow that for him; and there may be a man whom, if he were brought to me, I would have beaten.”

key_terms.أَبِي بَصِيرٍ: Abū Baṣīr, the narrator reporting the hadith
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.امْرَأَةٍ: a woman found with the man in the house
key_terms.لَأَجَزْتُ: I would permit or validate that claim for him
key_terms.لَضَرَبْتُهُ: I would have him beaten as a disciplinary punishment

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام treat a man and woman found together if they claim to be married?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a case involving a man and a woman claiming to be husband and wife when found together in private. The response of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام indicates that legal judgment may depend on surrounding circumstances and the credibility of the individuals involved, reflecting judicial discernment in matters of marriage and accusation.
